question: The Commission’s ‘Review of ongoing financial assistance for Palestine’ states that, for the PEGASE (Mécanisme Palestino-européen de Gestion de l’Aide Socio-économique) programme, ‘every individual recipient of EU funds (eligible civil servants, pensioners and heads of vulnerable families) is screened through available tools that can scan more than 1 500 sanction lists’. This screening is carried out by the Commission and ex ante auditors. 1.
Who are the ex ante auditors that scan the 1 500 sanctions lists, and what tools are used?
How many individuals in the Gaza Strip and in the West Bank are on the sanctions lists?

Considering that Hamas alone is estimated to have a military wing of 30 000-40 000 active members, to which 10 000 Palestinian Islamic Jihad members may be added, how do these numbers compare to the number of individuals included on the sanctions lists? In other words, what share of terrorists are filtered out through the sanctions lists?
answer: Under the PEGASE (Mécanisme Palestino-européen de Gestion de l’Aide Socio-économique) allocation an amount is reserved for safeguarding measures: audit, verification, monitoring, screening. The safeguards system includes audits (ex ante and ex post) procured to internationally recognised experts in the sector.

The checks are supported by available tools which can scan more than sanction lists, media records and information on politically exposed people and match them with the lists of beneficiaries. EU has adopted various sanctions targeting Hamas and related individuals and entities.

These designations are subject to an asset freeze and to whom no funds or economic resources can be made directly or indirectly available or made available for their benefit. This includes also via any possible EU financial assistance. Palestinian Islamic Jihad and Hamas-Izz al-Din al-Qassem have been on the EU terrorist list (1) since 2001 and Hamas in its entirety since 2003.

Following the 7 October 2023 terrorist attacks, the EU also added three Hamas related individuals under its terrorist list. In order to complement the existing counterterrorism framework, on 19 January 2024, the EU established a new dedicated sanctions regime (2) targeting mainly financiers of Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Currently six individuals are listed under this regime.

Furthermore, on 12 April 2024, the Council added three Hamas-related entities responsible for sexual and gender-based violence during the 7 October 2023 attacks under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime (3).
